items.subject: Physics
items.full_stem: A particle moving along a straight line with uniform acceleration covers a distance of $12\text{ m}$ during the $3^{\text{rd}}$ second of its motion and $20\text{ m}$ during the $5^{\text{th}}$ second of its motion. Assuming the particle started moving at $t = 0$, what is the total distance traveled by the particle in the first $4$ seconds?
items.stored_explanation_summary: Derives a=4 m/s², u=2 m/s correctly via s_n, then claims s=ut+½at²=8+32=48 m and keys B; incorrectly dismisses D=40 as a distractor.

independent_reasoning.proposition: Find displacement/distance in first 4 s under constant a, given distances in 3rd and 5th seconds.

option_analysis.B: incorrect as keyed — equals erroneous 8+32=48 arithmetic; not the physical result

items.ncert_section: 2.4 Kinematic equations for uniformly accelerated motion; summary kinematic equations (v=v0+at, x=v0 t + ½ a t²)
items.ncert_evidence: Class XI Physics Ch.2 presents uniformly accelerated kinematic equations used here. Distance-in-nth-second formula is a standard derived application of those equations; printed page numbers not claimed.
items.explanation_assessment: FAIL — u and a derivation correct; final arithmetic asserts 8+32=48 (false; 8+32=40). Explanation also mislabels correct option D as wrong.

original_fail_precise_reason.detail: Independent solution yields 40 m (option D). Stored answer B (48 m) mismatches. Explanation contains arithmetic error claiming 8+32=48. Not an NCERT contradiction; concept is NCERT-derived.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.full_stem: Consider the chemical species $\text{XeF}_5^-$, $\text{SF}_4$, and $\text{ICl}_3$. According to the VSEPR theory, which of the following correctly pairs each species with its molecular geometry (shape)?

stored_options.A: XeF5−: Pentagonal planar; SF4: See-saw; ICl3: T-shaped
stored_options.B: XeF5−: Pentagonal bipyramidal; SF4: Square planar; ICl3: Trigonal planar
stored_options.C: XeF5−: Square pyramidal; SF4: Tetrahedral; ICl3: Trigonal bipyramidal
stored_options.D: XeF5−: Pentagonal planar; SF4: Square planar; ICl3: T-shaped

items.stored_explanation_summary: XeF5− as AX5E2 → pentagonal planar; SF4 as AX4E → see-saw; ICl3 as AX3E2 → T-shaped.

independent_reasoning.proposition: Pair each of XeF5−, SF4, ICl3 with molecular shape under VSEPR.
independent_reasoning.XeF5_minus: Xe valence 8 + 5 F + 1 charge = 14 e− → 7 pairs → 5 bp + 2 lp (AX5E2). Electron geometry pentagonal bipyramidal; lone pairs axial → molecular shape pentagonal planar.
independent_reasoning.SF4: S 6 + 4 F = 10 e− → 5 pairs → 4 bp + 1 lp (AX4E) → see-saw.
independent_reasoning.ICl3: I 7 + 3 Cl = 10 e− → 5 pairs → 3 bp + 2 lp (AX3E2) → T-shaped.
independent_reasoning.note_on_option_B_XeF5: Pentagonal bipyramidal is the electron-pair geometry, not the molecular shape for AX5E2.

option_analysis.B: incorrect — confuses XeF5− molecular vs electron geometry; SF4 and ICl3 wrong
option_analysis.D: incorrect — SF4 is not square planar (XeF4 is)

items.ncert_section: VSEPR theory; Tables 4.6–4.8 (AB2–AB6; AB4E see-saw; AB3E2 T-shape); ClF3 in exercises; XeF2 mentioned only as noble-gas compound example (not XeF5−)
items.ncert_evidence: SF4/ICl3 shapes follow NCERT AB4E see-saw and AB3E2 T-shape patterns (ClF3 named). Full corpus keyword scan found no XeF5/XeF5− and no pentagonal planar molecular example. Table 4.6 covers AB2–AB6 without heptacoordinate AX5E2. Therefore the XeF5− claim is chemically standard but not directly located in authoritative StudyMaterial NCERT PDFs.
items.explanation_assessment: PASS chemically for stored answer A; terminology of electron vs molecular geometry for XeF5− is appropriate. NCERT-direct example support for XeF5− not established.

human_review_precise_reason.detail: Scientific answer MATCH and unique. Remaining barrier is NCERT support for XeF5− pentagonal planar (material to every option), not answer wrongness. Requires human NCERT/syllabus authorization decision — do not auto-promote to CERTIFIED.
